submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole fires when the current token closes a well-formed, expected constituent in a sentence that continues: the comma or semicolon sealing a coherent fronted temporal or clausal adjunct ('In 1969,', 'According to the report,', 'Once upon a time,'), or a noun that coherently fills an anticipated slot — a same-category enumeration member ('flour, one egg', 'Tokyo, Berlin', 'eight characters and one number'), a valid SELECT column ('SELECT name'), a range endpoint ('through Sunday'), or a selectionally fitting object ('the onions ... pan'). It stays near-silent when the same slot holds a semantically anomalous filler ('second garage,', 'Tokyo, apple', 'the rocks ... pan', 'SELECT table') or when the boundary punctuation is removed, and its output direction promotes ',' as the continuation marker.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The freighter left Rotterdam on schedule in early March. The crew completed safety drills before departure. Engineers inspected the main engine and auxiliary systems twice. Fuel bunkers were filled to capacity for the Atlantic crossing. Provisions were loaded into refrigerated holds below deck. The captain reviewed weather charts with the navigation officer. Satellite forecasts predicted moderate swells west of Ireland. Deck hands secured containers with additional lashing chains. Customs officials cleared all cargo manifests before midnight. The pilot boat escorted the vessel past the outer breakwater. Gulls followed the stern for several miles offshore. Watch rotations were posted in the mess hall. Apprentices studied charts under supervision of senior mates. The radio room tested emergency beacons on multiple frequencies. Morale remained high despite forecasts of rough seas. Crossing the North Sea took three uneventful days. Shetland appeared briefly through rain on the fourth morning. The convoy altered course to avoid fishing fleets near Rockall. Night watches logged passing tankers and distant trawlers. Maintenance crews repainted railings during calm intervals. The cook baked fresh bread whenever seas permitted. Medical supplies were inventoried and restocked from reserve lockers. Diesel filters were replaced during the mid ocean leg. A pod of whales surfaced alongside the port bow at sunrise. Photographs of the encounter were pinned in the crew lounge. Navigation fixes were plotted every four hours without fail. Gyrocompass error was checked against celestial sights nightly. The second mate trained cadets in sextant handling on deck. Storm shutters were tested ahead of forecast gales. Bilge pumps were run and inspected for debris. Insulation in cold stores was examined for frost damage. When the tide finally turned at dawn, harbor pilots guided freighters inward through the narrow channel toward the waiting berths. Pilots boarded by ladder near the sea buoy. Tugs made fast on both quarters promptly. Lines were passed to dock workers ashore. Cranes began discharging containers within the hour. Inspectors verified seals and weights against manifests. Refrigerated units were plugged into shore power immediately. The crew stood down to harbour watches for rest. Shore leave was granted in two rotating groups. Engineers began scheduled overhaul of pumps and valves. Bunkering barges arrived alongside before evening. Fresh water tanks were topped up overnight. Waste was offloaded under supervision of port authorities. The captain filed arrival reports with owners and agents. A new voyage plan was drafted for the return leg.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long-context holdout: the only comma seals a coherent fronted temporal adjunct buried deep in a comma-free voyage log.
